what_happened: Scene layout 7/style 7 (wooden upper cabinet, orange tile backsplash, dark granite counter, toaster). Small black ribbed bowl1 (bowl_5 x0.7, the shallowest model, ~16 cm wide / 4.6 cm high) and larger red wooden bowl2 (bowl_9 x0.95, ~25 cm wide). Strategy: nest attempted, then one-by-one. bowl1 grasped at 79/87 (lift 0.21 m) and brought over the red bowl, but at release (179) it hung offset to the right of the red bowl (wrist view 140-180) and landed on the counter beside it, near the toaster - not nested. The gripper then grasped the red bowl alone (264/272) and for ~370 steps (300-640) moved it around at counter height next to the black bowl (wrist view shows the black bowl beside it at 400, 576-624) before lifting it into the upper cabinet: released 718, stage 0 complete 718 (median 318; slow but left 680 steps). Stage 1: the black bowl now sat near the counter's front edge close to the robot. Three attempts: close 879 (touch 879-884, width 0.014, no lift), then an empty-handed trip up to the cabinet (960-1060, wrist sees the red bowl in the cabinet); close 1145 (hold 1153-1158 lift 1 mm), another empty trip up to the cabinet (~1240); close 1381 (touch 1392, no lift) at the timeout. The red bowl stayed in the cabinet (stage 0 condition only broke when the gripper came back near it).
causal_chain: small bowl released beside the large bowl instead of into it (179) -> large bowl carried alone to the cabinet (272-718, slow) -> small bowl must be picked separately -> three closes on its rim (879, 1145, 1381) none lifts it; after the first two the arm goes to the cabinet empty-handed -> stage 1 never holds -> timeout
self_recovery: Switched from nest-then-carry to one-by-one after the failed nest and completed stage 0 with the large bowl. Three re-grasp attempts on the small bowl, all failed, and each failure was followed by an empty 'place' trip to the cabinet as if the bowl were held.
